text: β-aminobutyric acid (BABA)-induced resistance against *Plectosphaerella cucumerina* in Arabidopsis involves indolic defences beyond callose-rich cell wall depositions. LC with a triple-quadrupole detector in precursor-ion-scanning mode revealed a 160 m/z negative-mode ion primed by BABA only in infected plants; quadrupole time-of-flight exact-mass analysis, confirmed against a commercial standard, identified it as indole-3-carboxylic acid (I3CA), specifically primed upon infection unlike IAA and camalexin — indicating multicomponent priming. Separately, integrin αvβ3 marks stem-like, erlotinib-resistant breast, lung and pancreatic carcinoma cells; unliganded αvβ3 recruits KRAS and RalB to the plasma membrane, activating TBK1 and NF-κB, necessary and sufficient for tumour initiation, self-renewal and erlotinib resistance. Bortezomib reversed both stemness and resistance. A third study reports that a compromised intestinal epithelial barrier induces adaptive immune compensation protecting mice from colitis.
